facts.F20: Test side only, behaviour-free. No production file, no Program.cs, no configuration key changes. Carrier owners: rule constants stay on their existing rule classes (ModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest, TrackerIntegrationModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest, Access and Licensing module boundaries tests); the module rule shapes stay on ModuleRules; Reports module boundaries get one new NUnit fixture ReportsModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest that holds its inline lists by full type name. Procedural-style static rule helpers are the repository convention for architecture tests; no new class is invented beyond the fixture and its made-up offender types.
facts.F21: Claim-to-checker: every claim here is a finite set comparison over the compiled IL (listed types equal measured types, listed edges equal measured edges, both ways) or a text sweep. Quint, TLA+ and Agda are not applicable: there is no state machine, no transition, no temporal or fairness claim and no unbounded input, so a model would restate the set comparison. The executable checker is the NUnit oracle itself on the compiled IL, with a made-up offender per rule and per list position as falsifier. Liveness: not applicable, nothing runs over time. Types: Mono.Cecil IL reading gives string full names, so a list entry is a string key, not a type; the made-up offenders prove each key position is live. Property testing: not applicable, the domains are finite and enumerated.
facts.F22: Measured baselines, re-measured from today's compiled IL (Release-equivalent IlDependencies read): Domain 3 types, Application 25 top-level types, Application.Metrics 8 types, 36 in all, ReportRepository the only Reports type left under Services. Domain reaches only Models (kernel) and System: R-RP2 exception list empty. Outside reaches Domain: 0 types, R-RP3 list empty. Outside reaches Application: API controllers and Program (allowed by role) plus ReportRepository: R-RP4 list holds 1. Application reaches Data, API, module Adapters, Tracker integration, RBAC, update code: none. EF Core: ReportBulkCommands -> DbUpdateException, ReportBulkRemover -> DbUpdateException: R-RP5 list holds 2. R-RP6 list holds 12 edges: DailySeriesSummary -> FlowMetrics.Domain.PercentileCalculator; ReportCommands and ReportQueries -> Licensing.Application.ILicenseService; ReportOwnerLookup, TeamReportMetricSeries and PortfolioReportMetricSeries -> Services.Interfaces.Repositories.IRepository1; six types (PortfolioReportMetricSeries, ReportBulkCommands, ReportCommands, ReportQueries, TeamReportMetricSeries, ThenAndNowTemplate) -> Platform.Host.ILighthouseClock. Flow metrics Application edges (TeamReportMetricSeries -> ITeamMetricsService, PortfolioReportMetricSeries -> IPortfolioMetricsService) are legal conformist edges and not listed.

Exact-path exclusions only: feature A measurement files that must spell old names (ReportsMembership.cs, ReportsMembershipArchUnitTest.cs, and any fixture they use), the sweep oracle itself (builds old names from segments), and RefinementRulesNameOnlyTheModuleArchUnitTest.cs, whose frozen made-up offender names Reports as a group member of the old Services alternation. Feature A's three helper files ReportsRulesSeeTheMoveArchUnitTest.cs, ReportsPatternRoles.cs and ReportsStringsTheMoveRenames.cs assert old-or-new sight and an old-path rename list; after the move they are settled and removed by the crafter, as feature C of the previous package did, and ReportsLivesInItsModuleArchUnitTest drops its rename-list tests. Every other Reports rule keeps its verdict.
facts.F25: No rule or list is loosened: lists are inline by full type name, compared both ways, only shrink. Rules read the compiled IL, never an empty set: each rule asserts its subject set is not empty. Outer types only for set comparison (strip the part after plus). A rule exemption is exact per type, never a namespace or layer. Failures use Reports own wording (ModuleWording Reports, the API). No nWave scenario tags in code. No edit to an approved oracle of this feature after approval; one oracle file per slice.
facts.F26: Input bounds: no stored or validated input is introduced. Test budgets: default per-test budget, the IL read is shared per fixture (Lazy ModuleDefinition disposed in OneTimeTearDown); no derogation requested.
